[1/4] Plan: lineage drift observability - per-species genetic distance to its founder, near-speciation count and trophic split in analytics, the CLI species/stats reports and the observatory payload/table; tests first

impact_assessment.why: Speciation is the project's headline mechanic, yet operators cannot see how far a living lineage has drifted from its founder or how close it is to splitting; only raw populations and global trait means are exposed.
impact_assessment.benefits: Turns the fossil record into a drift dashboard: the CLI and observatory surface each lineage's mean and worst drift as a fraction of the speciation threshold, plus herbivore/carnivore split and age, so a run's radiation is legible before the split happens.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: additive analytics API, CLI lines and JSON keys; determinism: no engine or RNG change; dependency: stdlib only (genome.genetic_distance); concurrency: read-only payload built under the server lock; state: no save-schema change, no persisted fields.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Leave every existing token, JSON key and table column in place; compute metrics in a pure function over the current population; prove determinism is untouched by re-running the existing replay and save round-trip tests in the Phase 4 gate.

[1/3] Plan: guard the drift-share division in the CLI reports so a save with species_distance 0.0 renders 'no positive threshold' instead of raising ZeroDivisionError; regression test first

impact_assessment.why: Review of the lineage-drift commit found that save.py accepts a zero speciation distance, after which stats and repl species crash with an uncaught ZeroDivisionError.
impact_assessment.benefits: Restores the readable Why:/Fix: command-line contract for every save the loader accepts and closes the review finding.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: CLI text only, JSON and save schema untouched; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: no persisted fields.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Confine the change to one helper plus the two report sites, keep the existing percentage text for positive thresholds, and prove it with a failing-first regression test plus the full Phase 4 gate.

[1/5] Plan the interactive observatory UI and one-click launchers: a live control bar (new world, play/pause, step, speed), /live and /step.json endpoints over one session, static app.css/app.js, start.py + start.bat/start.sh/start.command with browser auto-open, docs, ADR and tests.

impact_assessment.why: The user asked for a UI and a one-click start; the observatory is only reachable through CLI flags and reloads the whole page to advance.
impact_assessment.benefits: Operators can create a world, play it, pause, step it and fire shocks from one page after double-clicking a launcher.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: existing HTML tokens, JSON payloads, save format and determinism must survive; dependency: none beyond the stdlib; concurrency: session resets and steps stay under the handler lock; state: a /new reset must not mutate a caller's save unexpectedly.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep the server-rendered dashboard as the single source, add fragment and JSON endpoints beside it, guard every engine touch with the existing lock, preserve all current routes and tokens, and cover resets, refusals and launchers with tests.
